div.head: Wi 9
div.ab: Gif esne ofer dryhtnes hæse þeowweorc wyrce an sunnan æfen efter hire setlgange oþ monan æfenes setlgang, LXXX scll' se dryhtne gebete.
Gif esne ofer dryhtnes hæse þeowweorc wyrce an sunnan æfen efter hire setlgange oþ monan æfenes setlgang, LXXX scætta se dryhtne gebete.
Gif esne of(er) dryhtnes hæse þoewweorc wyrce an sunnan æfen efter hire setlgange oþ monan æfenes setlgang, LXXX scƚƚ se dryhten gebete.
Wenn ein Lohnknecht auf des Herrn Geheiss Sklavenarbeit thut am Sonnabend nach Sonnenuntergang bis zum Untergang des Mon[tagsvor]abends, [so] büsse jener Herr 80 Schll. [dem Könige].
If a hired servant does slave-labour at his lord’s command on Saturday after sunset until the setting of Mon[day’s eve], [then] let that lord pay 80 shillings [to the king].
If a servant, contrary to his lord’s command, does servile work between sunset on Saturday evening and sunset on Sunday evening, he shall pay 80 sceattas to his lord.
If a servant, by his lord’s command, do servile work between sunset on Saturday evening and sunset on Sunday evening, his lord is to pay 80 shillings.
If a servant according to his lord’s order does slave-work after sunset on the eve of Sunday until sunset on the eve of Monday, let the lord pay 80 shillings [?sceattas].

Vgl. Gl unfrei 1e. 14c; Sonntag 2ff. Wi 9—11 stammt aus demselben Sinne, und wohl dem identischen, vermutlich Lateinischen Kanon einer Englischen Synode, wie Ine 3 bis 3, 2. Die Kapitel Wi 9—15 strafen Sonntagsentheiligung, Götzendienst und Fastenbruch, Einen Abschnitt bildend

Cf. Gl unfrei 1e. 14c; Sonntag 2ff. Wi 9—11 derives from the same spirit as Ine 3 to 3, 2, and probably from the identical, presumably Latin, canon of an English synod. The chapters Wi 9—15 punish desecration of Sunday, idolatry and breach of fasts, forming a single section

ofer (s. Wb 12) halte ich für Schreibfehler statt of; s. ebd. Parallelen. Die Gefahr lag nahe, da das Auge vom f den Haken rechts oben leicht als das Abkürzungszeichen für -er irrig ansehen konnte. Diese Bed. von of belegen Toller s. v. III—V; Koch Hist. Gram. II § 419. Dass ofer ‘wegen, durch’, die Ursache bezeichnen könne, find ich nur nach Verben des Affekts: ic blissige ofer þinre spræce Psalm 118; hia wundradon ofer hine Marc. 12, 17; ic miltsa ofer 8, 2: keine Parallelen zu dem hier notwendigen Sinne. Österreich nur sagt ‘über [auf] Befehl’. Schmids Emendation be, nach Ine 3, liegt graphisch zu fern. Schon Wilkins (Concilia, nicht in Leges, die contra übersetzen) verstand ex mandato. Thorpe, dem Stubbs Councils III 235 und Toller s. v. esne folgen, verteidigt den Sinn ‘gegen’: in c. 9 handle der Knecht gegen des Herrn ausdrückliches Arbeitsverbot, in 10 nur ohne solches, beide Male also freiwillig. Dagegen spricht: A. die Öffentlichkeit kümmert sich wohl um Sonntagsbruch, aber nicht um des Knechtes Ungehorsam, den der Herr allein strafen mag. B. Dass ein Knecht 80 Schilling zahlen könne (⁴/₅ Freien-Wergeld), ist ausgeschlossen; selbst für Fastenbruch und Götzenopfer zahlt er nur 6 Schill.; Wi 13. 15. C. Andere Gesetze scheiden wohl die freiwillige Sünde von der vom Herrn gebotenen, auch besonders im Bruche des Feiertags (s. d. Gl 5a—e), aber nicht die vom Herrn verbotene Sünde von der durch ihn nicht gebotenen. D. Die Arbeit heisst ‘Fron’, sie geschieht für den Herrn; welcher Sklave tat solche gegen des Herrn Verbot? E. Zu his rade (aus freiem Willen des Knechtes, 10) in Ggs. steht vermutlich hier, wie zu his ræde 15, die Veranlassung durch den Herrn; und dieser Fall würde, falls ofer ‘gegen’ richtig wäre, gerade bei der Fron fehlen

ofer (see Wb 12) I take to be a scribal error for of; see the parallels ibid. The danger was close at hand, since the eye could easily mistake the hook at the upper right of the f for the abbreviation mark for -er. This meaning of of is attested by Toller s. v. III—V; Koch Hist. Gram. II § 419. That ofer, ‘because of, through’, could denote the cause I find only after verbs of emotion: ic blissige ofer þinre spræce Psalm 118; hia wundradon ofer hine Marc. 12, 17; ic miltsa ofer 8, 2: no parallels to the sense required here. Only in Austria does one say ‘über [auf] Befehl’. Schmid’s emendation be, after Ine 3, is graphically too remote. Already Wilkins (Concilia; not in the Leges, which translate contra) understood ex mandato. Thorpe, whom Stubbs Councils III 235 and Toller s. v. esne follow, defends the sense ‘against’: in c. 9, he argues, the servant acts against his lord’s express prohibition of work, in 10 merely without such a prohibition, thus in both cases voluntarily. Against this: A. the public authority does indeed concern itself with Sunday-breaking, but not with the servant’s disobedience, which the lord alone may punish. B. That a servant could pay 80 shillings (⁴/₅ of a freeman’s wergild) is out of the question; even for breach of fast and sacrifice to idols he pays only 6 shill.; Wi 13. 15. C. Other laws do indeed distinguish voluntary sin from sin commanded by the lord, especially in the breach of holy days too (see that word in Gl 5a—e), but not sin forbidden by the lord from sin not commanded by him. D. The work is called ‘labour service’; it is done for the lord; what slave would have done such work against his lord’s prohibition? E. The contrast to his rade (of the servant’s own free will, 10) is presumably here, as with his ræde 15, instigation by the lord; and this case, if ofer ‘against’ were correct, would be missing precisely for labour service

Vgl. Frige-æfen (Frigeniht ‘Thursday night’ Napier Old Engl. lex. 26), Sæterniht, Sunnan niht (Ælfric Hom. I 216). Doch ist hier der ganze Tag vorher, nicht der Abend allein gemeint, sonst wäre der einschränkende Zusatz ‘von Sonnenuntergang’ unnütz; vgl. Wb: Mona 3

Cf. Frige-æfen (Frigeniht ‘Thursday night’ Napier Old Engl. lex. 26), Sæterniht, Sunnan niht (Ælfric Hom. I 216). Here, however, the whole day before is meant, not the evening alone; otherwise the restricting addition ‘from sunset’ would be pointless; cf. Wb: Mona 3
Über diese Erstreckung des Sonntags s. d. Gl 2
On this extension of Sunday see that word in Gl 2
Wiederum sieht Schmid richtig, der Herr müsse der Zahler sein, s. o. Erkl. 2B. Ebenso hat die Hs. -ne statt -en in unlægen Wi 16. 21
Here again Schmid rightly sees that the lord must be the one who pays; see above note 2B. Likewise the MS has -ne instead of -en in unlægen Wi 16. 21

Das Strafgeld bei Ine ist zwar viel kleiner, allein dort kommt die Freilassung des Knechts hinzu. Der König erhält das Strafgeld als Gebieter der Sonntagsruhe. Spätere Gesetze geben es dem Bischofe wenigstens teilweise; s. Gl Feiertag 5a—f

The fine in Ine is indeed much smaller, but there the freeing of the slave is added. The king receives the fine as the one who commands Sunday rest. Later laws give it, at least in part, to the bishop; see Gl Feiertag 5a—f

note.label: scætta
note.seg: scll'. H.

The slight emendation of ‘shilling’ to ‘sceatt’ (possibly due to a misunderstanding of the abbreviation sc.) gives an intelligible sense. Liebermann emends ofer to of and dryhtne to dryhten, and thus makes the lord liable to the penalty of 80 shillings, while in cap. 10 he takes rade in the sense of ræde, which really seems to necessitate a third emendation. His explanation however involves too great a discrepancy between cap. 9 and Ine, cap. 3; for then a fine of 1600 coins would be required for an offence for which contemporary West Saxon law prescribes a fine of only 120 (or 150) equivalent coins. Even if the value of the slave is added the total sum will only be 360 (or 450) coins. Moreover the healsfang, specified as a fine due from a freeman for a similar offence, must have been far less than 80 shillings, whether we equate it with the sum specified in Abt. cap. 22, or not, whereas in Ine, cap. 3 § 2 the freeman is liable to a heavier penalty.

note.label: servant
note.seg: esne, here and in chap. 10. see p. 393, n. 8

note.label: shillings
note.seg: Accepting, as against my first edition, Liebermann’s rendering, which takes ofer “against” as error for of “by”, and se dryhtne as error for se dryhten. Attenborough replaced shillings by sceattas, to be paid by the servant to his lord, but sums are not stated in sceattas when they are a round number of shillings. With Attenborough’s reading we hear nothing of the penalty incurred by the lord who orders his servant to work.

note.label: of(er)
note.seg: Liebermann, correctly in my opinion, suggests emending this to of; he postulates that the cross-bar of the f may have been mistaken for an extension stroke representing -er.

note.label: dryhten
note.seg: This clause is grammatically corrupt; manuscript reads se dryhtne. See discussion under ‘Transgressing the laws of the church’ in Commentary.

note.label: to
note.seg: See note b to the Old English text. I have translated as if the text read of, ‘according to,’ rather than ofer, ‘against,’ as the meaning of this clause is in opposition to the following clause. See discussion under ‘Transgressing the laws of the church’ in Commentary.

note.label: Monday,
note.seg: That is, work is forbidden from Saturday’s sunset to Sunday’s sunset.

note.label: [?sceattas].
note.seg: This clause is grammatically corrupt; translation follows Liebermann’s emendations, with a possible change of shillings to sceattas to correct for the unreasonably stiff fine. See discussion under ‘Transgressing the laws of the church’ in Commentary.
